question: What is the primary abnormal protein found in the red blood cells of a person with sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: The genetic mutation in sickle cell anaemia specifically leads to the production of abnormal haemoglobin S, which changes the shape of the red blood cells when it loses oxygen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: Why do red blood cells change into a sickle shape in this condition?

options.A: The bone marrow produces cells with too much iron and water inside them
options.B: Haemoglobin S molecules stick together to form rigid rods when they release oxygen
options.C: White blood cells attack and deform the healthy red blood cells
options.D: Excess sugar in the bloodstream causes the red blood cells to shrink and warp

explanation: When haemoglobin S delivers oxygen to body tissues, it clumps into stiff strands that distort the normal round cell into a crescent shape. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: What genotype represents a person who carries the sickle cell trait without having the full disease?
explanation: Genotype AS means the individual has one normal gene and one mutated gene, making them a healthy carrier of the trait. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: What must happen for a child to be born with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Only the mother needs to have the full sickle cell disease
options.B: The child must be exposed to severe malaria during infancy
options.C: Both parents must pass on a copy of the mutated sickle cell gene
options.D: Either parent must have genotype AS while the other has genotype AA

explanation: Because it is an autosomal recessive condition, a child needs two copies of the abnormal gene, requiring both parents to contribute a sickle gene. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: What is the medical term for the yellowing of the skin and eyes caused by the rapid breakdown of red blood cells?
explanation: Jaundice happens when red blood cells break down quickly, releasing excess bilirubin which the liver processes more slowly than it is produced. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h3)

question: Why are children with sickle cell anaemia at a much higher risk of severe bacterial infections?

options.A: Low dietary iron intake weakens the entire immune system from birth
options.B: The bone marrow stops producing white blood cells to make more sickled cells
options.C: Repeated blood vessel blockages eventually damage and destroy spleen function
options.D: Abnormal haemoglobin coats bacteria and prevents immune cells from seeing them

explanation: The spleen filters bacteria and helps fight infections, but repeated sickling clogs its vessels until it stops working entirely, a process called auto-splenectomy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h3)

question: What is the most common trigger for a vaso-occlusive pain crisis in a patient with sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: Dehydration thickens the blood and infections increase physical stress, both of which easily trigger blood cells to sickle and block vessels. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h4)

question: A patient with sickle cell anaemia is admitted in a painful vaso-occlusive crisis. Which immediate nursing intervention should be prioritized?

options.A: Preparing the patient for immediate surgical removal of the spleen
options.B: Restricting fluid intake to prevent fluid overload in the lungs
options.C: Administering prescribed pain medication and encouraging fluids
options.D: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to improve circulation

explanation: Managing pain and rehydrating the patient to thin the blood and restore circulation are the immediate priorities during an acute crisis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h4)

question: Which laboratory test is considered the gold standard for confirming a diagnosis of sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: Haemoglobin electrophoresis separates the different types of haemoglobin proteins to provide a definitive diagnosis of the specific genotype. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h5)

question: What does an elevated reticulocyte count in a routine blood test usually indicate in a patient with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Iron supplements are building up to toxic levels in the blood
options.B: The patient is experiencing a sudden kidney infection
options.C: The spleen has successfully cleared all abnormal cells from circulation
options.D: The bone marrow is working hard to replace destroyed red blood cells

explanation: Reticulocytes are newly formed red blood cells. A high count shows the bone marrow is rushing to make new cells to make up for those lost to haemolysis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h5)

question: Why is malaria prevention especially critical for individuals living with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Anti-malarial medications cure the underlying genetic mutation permanently
options.B: Malaria infection triggers severe red blood cell sickling and life-threatening crises
options.C: Malaria parasites feed directly on normal adult haemoglobin A exclusively
options.D: Fever from malaria permanently stops the bone marrow from making blood

explanation: Fever, inflammation, and red blood cell destruction caused by malaria are powerful triggers that induce widespread vessel blockage in sickle cell patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h6)

question: What is the main reason young children with sickle cell anaemia are given daily prophylactic penicillin?

options.A: To prevent severe bacterial infections due to reduced spleen function
options.B: To stop malaria parasites from entering the bloodstream during the rainy season
options.C: To stimulate the bone marrow to produce more flexible red blood cells
options.D: To reduce chronic joint pain caused by dactylitis in the fingers and toes

explanation: Because the spleen loses its ability to filter bacteria early in life, daily penicillin protects these children from dangerous encapsulated bacterial infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h6)

question: Which lifestyle advice is most important for a nurse to emphasize during patient education for sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake in the evening to prevent frequent nighttime urination
options.B: Maintain consistent daily hydration and avoid extreme temperature changes
options.C: Wear tight, supportive clothing to keep the peripheral blood vessels compressed
options.D: Engage in intense competitive sports to build strong cardiovascular endurance

explanation: Drinking plenty of water prevents the blood from thickening, and avoiding cold temperatures stops blood vessels from narrowing, both of which prevent crises. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h7)

question: A mother brings her young child with sickle cell anaemia to the clinic. Which statement by the mother shows she understands home care instructions?

options.A: We stopped the daily penicillin because our child has not been sick lately
options.B: We avoid letting our child eat any green vegetables containing folic acid
options.C: I only give pain medication when the swelling in the fingers becomes unbearable
options.D: I make sure my child drinks plenty of water every day, even when feeling well

explanation: Consistent daily hydration keeps red blood cells flowing smoothly and is a cornerstone of preventing painful vaso-occlusive episodes at home. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h7)

question: What is the term for the bone tissue death in the hip or shoulder caused by blocked blood supply in sickle cell patients?
explanation: Avascular necrosis occurs when restricted blood flow deprives bone tissue of oxygen and nutrients, causing the bone to break down over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h8)

question: Why is regular multi-disciplinary follow-up essential for adults living with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: To monitor and manage progressive long-term damage to major body organs
options.B: To perform routine blood transfusions that reverse the abnormal gene sequence
options.C: To prevent the patient from ever experiencing another painful crisis again
options.D: To ensure the patient takes daily antibiotics to cure the genetic mutation

explanation: Chronic organ damage to the kidneys, lungs, brain, and joints accumulates over years, requiring coordinated specialist care to catch and treat complications early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h8)
